newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate end up on late speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate end up on late speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 50 basis points at 24.50 percent on Monday following a late speculative surge by big players with ample liquidity, traders said.
"Those with liquidity are putting pressure on the market, they are very few and are in the driving seat right now," a trader said.

The trader noted the central bank drained substantial liquidity through secondary auctions which it assigned at high rates due to pressure from a small number of banks that have most of the cash available in the market.
The central bank drained a hefty 9.490 billion pesos from the system through seven auctions, which it assigned at rates of between 26.40-28.70 percent.

"Banco de Mexico is greatly rewarding players with cash and there is much market speculation," the trader added. "The daily secondary auction is supposed to be representative, but it isn't because only those with liquidity take part and there is no one else to lower rates."
A money market analyst said: "The market is not acting in line with domestic fundamentals. There is nothing to explain upside pressure on rates other than speculation."

Traders said market fears of a sell-off in the U.S. bond market in the wake of possible strong consumer price data on Tuesday were not sufficient to explain the gain in secondary rates during Monday's session.

"If investors were really scared of hikes in U.S. rates, then they would already have withdrawn their money, but the peso has not responded to that. Foreigners are not bailing out and they are not putting domestic rates under pressure," another trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.2 of a centavo weaker at 7.9180/7.9200 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 1/32 to yield 7.17 percent in late trade.
Dealers said the outlook of increased primary rates for the third consecutive week on Tuesday may also have exerted some upside pressure on secondary market rates.
Overnight rates on bank paper also succumbed to speculation and ended up 150 basis points at 26.50 percent.
On the Cetes futures market in Chicago, June contracts fell 46 centavos to close at 77.33 pesos.
Liquidity of 4.518 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
